sections.title: SHAPE THE UNDERGROUND.
sections.intro: Excavation changes the world you move through. Your passages, tracks and facilities persist between visits, so the next trip starts with the work you have already done.

cards.title: Dig, fill and explore
paragraphs: Break through soil and mineral deposits, fill terrain when you need to reshape a passage, and use jumping and rope climbing to move through the side-view mine. Digging beneath a track can change it into a vertical rope, so the ground beneath your route matters.

cards.title: Pack for the return
paragraphs: Arrange and rotate shaped items in your grid backpack to make room for minerals, creature parts and supplies. Keep an eye on the miner's moisture: it drains over time and from creature damage, and contact with molten plasma restores it.

sections.note: Digging, filling, track work and player construction do not spend player stamina in the current design. Materials and legal placement still matter.

sections.title: BUILD A NETWORK THAT WORKS.
sections.intro: Connect freight routes to gathering facilities and an exit. Stations can pass cargo through powered relay stations, but materials reach town storage only when a cart actually arrives at a real exit.

cards.title: Stations + Dudu
paragraphs: Each station has its own permanent Dudu cart. With cargo, power and a valid route, it loads and delivers automatically, then returns for more. It waits when empty and pauses while you arrange that station's inventory.

cards.title: Minefields
paragraphs: These gathering facilities collect eligible ore in their service area. A station cart can collect their stock when the facilities are connected by a valid powered rail route.

cards.title: Power stations
paragraphs: Tap electric-source regions and carry power along electrified tracks. Connected facilities share the circuit's capacity. If their combined demand exceeds supply, all consumers on that circuit pause until enough capacity is available.

cards.title: Built rift exits
paragraphs: Construct powered rift exits to connect travel between powered exits. They are one of the mine's functional building choices, alongside stations, minefields and power stations.

sections.note: The mine keeps producing and transporting while you are in town and while game time advances through rest or a market. This is an active game-world clock; there is no offline income or offline time progression.

sections.eyebrow: FROM RAW MATERIAL TO SOMETHING PLAYFUL
sections.title: MAKE TOYS. STOCK THE STALL.
sections.intro: The workshop turns the materials you bring home into finished stock. Your choice of recipes gives each expedition a purpose: gather what the next batch needs, rather than sell raw ore for money.

cards.title: A first sample teaches the recipe
paragraphs: Time the assembly action while the needle is in the gold zone. Three successful steps complete the sample and learn the recipe. A miss does not spend materials; the ingredient set is charged when the sample succeeds.
Once learned, the recipe skips that sample minigame and supports batch quantities. Finished toys can then be selected for an evening market.

cards.title: Two kinds of lasting progress
paragraphs: Recipe upgrades change the value of newly made stock; existing toys keep their original quality. Separately, permanent building research at Marksa's town workshop applies to every existing and future building of the same kind.
Higher-level stations and minefields handle higher-level materials, linking workshop research back to your underground network.

sections.recipeNote: A few mineral-only recipes to try. Each ingredient set makes one toy; other recipes also use creature materials.

sections.eyebrow: THE OTHER HALF OF THE ADVENTURE
sections.title: SELL A LITTLE MISCHIEF.
sections.intro: An evening market is an active shift. You move through the stalls, meet customers and keep service moving while their patience runs down.

cards.title: Choose what to bring
paragraphs: Select finished toys before opening. Shoppers show a request for a specific toy, so a varied stock gives you different requests to serve. Unsold toys remain in your inventory after the shift.

cards.title: Guide, make, collect
paragraphs: Recruit a shopper and lead them to your stall. On-site making begins after their arrival, with one toy prepared at a time. Handover and payment are separate: return to the customer and collect their payment with F before patience expires.

cards.title: Find your rhythm
paragraphs: Assign a Maker and Promoters to help with production and recruitment. Time a toy-horn promotion to reach more shoppers; a blast that is too loud can drive them away. At settlement, sales, tips and attending staff's wages determine the shift's profit.

sections.note: Successful sales feed Marksa's Evil Broadcast Tower. A stronger signal attracts more humans, and themed markets give you a reason to prepare particular toys. More stock, better service and the next mining trip become parts of the same plan.

sections.eyebrow: YOUR STRATEGY STARTS BEFORE THE MATCH
sections.title: PROGRAM YOUR NEXT MOVE.
sections.intro: You take the role of a super AI in a post-apocalyptic world, programming a robot squad to compete for resources. The modular chip system is the centre of the build: combine chip actions to create the behaviours you want to test.

cards.title: Choose chips for the board
paragraphs: The current release trailer shows a chip shop beside the hexagonal programming board. Choose modular actions, arrange a build around your combatant and take that setup into battle.

cards.title: Give the combination a purpose
paragraphs: Modular actions allow different tactical builds. Treat the arrangement as one plan: decide what you want your robot to do, try a combination that expresses that idea, and use the match to judge whether it works.

cards.title: Choose a battle stance
paragraphs: Battle stances add another choice to the build. The release trailer shows stance effects that change cooldown behaviour or which actions can trigger. Pick one to support the plan, then check what happens in the arena.

sections.eyebrow: WATCH YOUR DECISIONS MEET AN OPPONENT
sections.title: LET YOUR BUILD DO THE TALKING.
sections.intro: Quick, complex turn-based matches put your choices to the test. Preparation and testing connect directly: the chips you choose become a strategy to evaluate against the next arena challenge.

cards.title: Read the result
paragraphs: Arena screenshots place the combatants alongside health bars and visible chip boards. Follow those changing battle states and compare the outcome with the plan you built. Did the combination produce the behaviour you were aiming for?

cards.title: Carry a question into the next build
paragraphs: A match is feedback for the next experiment. Reconsider a chip choice or the overall combination, then test again. The game's iterative strategy testing is about experimenting, optimizing and validating your tactics through play.

sections.title: RETHINK. RERUN. RISE.
sections.intro: Circuit Stance is a strategy roguelike with a tiered scoring system. Victories move your rank upward; losses bring challenges and the risk of starting over.

cards.title: One useful testing cycle
paragraphs: Start with a chip arrangement, take it into a match, observe the result, and revise the build before another test. Compare what happened after the change, rather than assuming a new combination must be better.

cards.title: Progress through tactical learning
paragraphs: Ranking gives each encounter weight, while repeated testing helps you understand your build. The next decision can draw on the last battle: which ideas held up, which need another attempt, and what to change for the next opponent.

sections.note: The game’s flat 2D robot world has plenty of personality. The current release trailer shows a Hall of Fame scene alongside chip programming, battle stances and arena encounters.
